title: A Day in Your Courts
subtitle: Psalms 73–106 in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
This volume brings together Books Three and Four of the Psalter. Book Three begins with a man nearly losing his faith until he walks into God's house, and holds the darkest psalm in the Bible. Book Four opens with Moses's prayer about numbering our days and rises into songs where rivers clap and trees sing.

The volume answers them one at a time, thirty-four short poems in four parts, each beside a picture and under a single line from the psalm it answers. It follows Planted by the Water and As the Deer.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Keep the Psalms open alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Until I Entered
parts.epigraph: God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
parts.lightHint: Near 'until I walked in' (Psalm 73:13–26) in Part 1: Until I Entered

parts.title: A Day in Your Courts
parts.epigraph: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand.
parts.lightName: Light of A Day in Your Courts
parts.lightHint: Near 'open wide' (Psalm 81:10–16) in Part 2: A Day in Your Courts

parts.title: Our Dwelling Place
parts.epigraph: Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations.
parts.lightHint: Near 'count our days' (Psalm 90:1–12) in Part 3: Our Dwelling Place

parts.title: Bless the Lord, O My Soul
parts.epigraph: Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits
parts.lightName: Light of Bless the Lord, O My Soul
parts.lightHint: Near 'clap' (Psalm 98:7–9) in Part 4: Bless the Lord, O My Soul

paintings.title: until I walked in
paintings.epigraph: “until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered their latter end.”
paintings.poem:
the wicked were rich.
healthy. untroubled.
and I kept my heart clean
for nothing,
Asaph says.

it made no sense—
until I walked into God's house.

then I saw
the end of the story.

and this:
whom have I in heaven but you?
my heart may fail.
you are my portion
forever.

paintings.title: the day is yours
paintings.epigraph: “The day is yours, the night is also yours.”
paintings.poem:
the sanctuary was burned.
the signs were gone.
no prophet left.

and still:

the day is yours.
the night is yours too.
summer and winter—
you made them.

when everything else is ash,
the sun still comes up
on his schedule.

paintings.title: near
paintings.epigraph: “We give thanks, for your Name is near.”
paintings.poem:
we give thanks—
your name is near.

not far off in the clouds.
near.

close enough to call.
close enough to whisper.

paintings.title: broken arrows
paintings.epigraph: “Surely the wrath of man praises you.”
paintings.poem:
he broke the flashing arrows,
the shield, the sword,
the weapons of war.

and even human rage
ends up
serving his praise.

nothing people throw at God
is wasted.
he turns it
into a song.

paintings.title: no footprints
paintings.epigraph: “Your way was through the sea; your paths through the great waters. Your footsteps were not known.”
paintings.poem:
I couldn't sleep.
I couldn't speak.
has God forgotten?

then I remembered
the old wonders,
the road through the sea.

and this:
your footprints
weren't seen.

he led them through
without leaving a mark.

just because you can't see his tracks
doesn't mean
he isn't walking ahead.

paintings.title: tell the children
paintings.epigraph: “W e will not hide them from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of Y ahweh”
paintings.poem:
the longest history lesson
in the Psalms:
seventy-two verses
of what God did,
and how we forgot.

and the reason it's written:
so the children
will know,
and set their hope in God,
and not forget.

tell them the stories—
the good ones
and the hard ones.

paintings.title: for your name's sake
paintings.epigraph: “Help us, God of our salvation, for the glory of your name.”
paintings.poem:
help us—
not because we deserve it.

for your name's sake.

forgive us—
not because we've earned it.

for your name's sake.

when you have nothing left to plead,
plead his name.
it has never
been turned down.

paintings.title: turn us again
paintings.epigraph: “Turn us again, God. Cause your face to shine, and we will be saved.”
paintings.poem:
you brought a vine out of Egypt,
planted it,
and it filled the land.

now the walls are broken
and the wild boar tramples it.

three times the chorus comes back,
each time a little more desperate:

turn us again.
make your face shine,
and we'll be saved.

that's the whole prayer.
it's enough.

paintings.title: open wide
paintings.epigraph: “Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.”
paintings.poem:
open your mouth wide,
and I'll fill it—

like a nest of baby birds,
beaks wide,
nothing held back.

and at the end:
I would have fed you
the finest wheat,
honey from the rock.

he wants to give.
we keep our mouths
half closed.

paintings.title: the job description
paintings.epigraph: “Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless.”
paintings.poem:
God stands up
in the council of the powerful
and asks:
how long will you judge unjustly?

defend the weak.
the poor.
the fatherless.

that's the job description
of anyone
with power.

paintings.title: that they may know
paintings.epigraph: “you alone, whose name is Yahweh, are the Most High over all the earth.”
paintings.poem:
the nations made a pact,
a long list of enemies
in one alliance.

and the prayer
isn't only: defeat them.

it's: let them seek your name.
let them know
you alone
are God.

even for enemies,
the psalm's hope
is that they'd find out
who he is.

paintings.title: the sparrow's nest
paintings.epigraph: “Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars”
paintings.poem:
how lovely is your house.

even the sparrow
found a place there—
a little nest
tucked in the stones
near the altar.

if God makes room
for sparrows,
there's a place
for you.

and on the way there,
passing through the valley of weeping,
they make it
a place of springs.

paintings.title: they kissed
paintings.epigraph: “Mercy and truth meet together. Righteousness and peace have kissed each other.”
paintings.poem:
mercy and truth
meet on the road.

righteousness and peace
kiss.

we keep them apart—
truth without mercy,
peace without justice.

in God
they were never
strangers.

paintings.title: one piece
paintings.epigraph: “Make my heart undivided to fear your name.”
paintings.poem:
teach me your way,
and unite my heart.

I'm pulled in so many directions—
fear and hope,
God and money,
yes and maybe.

gather me up.
make me
one piece,
facing you.

paintings.title: all my springs
paintings.epigraph: “All my springs are in you.”
paintings.poem:
a short, strange psalm
about Zion,
and the foreigners
who'll be counted as born there—

Egypt, Babylon,
Philistia, Tyre, Cush.

and the singers and the dancers
say one thing:

all my springs
are in you.

paintings.title: still praying
paintings.epigraph: “In the morning, my prayer comes before you.”
paintings.poem:
this is the darkest psalm.
it doesn't end
with a turn to hope.

the last word is
darkness.

and it's in the Bible anyway.

sometimes that's all the prayer
you've got:
I'm still here, Lord.
it's morning again,
and I'm still praying.

that counts.
that's faith too.

paintings.title: the first line and the last
paintings.epigraph: “I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever.”
paintings.poem:
it begins in song:
I'll sing of your love forever.

then asks
why the crown lies in the dust.

and it ends Book Three
with a blessing anyway:
blessed be the Lord
forever.
amen and amen.

sometimes you sing
the first line
and the last line
without understanding
the middle.

paintings.title: count our days
paintings.epigraph: “So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.”
paintings.poem:
the oldest psalm,
a prayer of Moses.

Lord, you've been our home
for every generation.

we are grass—
green in the morning,
dry by evening.

so teach us
to count our days—

not to be afraid.
to be wise.

paintings.title: under his feathers
paintings.epigraph: “He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge.”
paintings.poem:
dwell in the shelter.
rest in the shadow.

under his feathers,
under his wings.

not a fortress of stone.
a mother bird's wing,
warm,
close,
covering.

and at the end, God speaks:
I will be with him
in trouble.

paintings.title: still green
paintings.epigraph: “They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green”
paintings.poem:
the righteous will flourish
like a palm tree,
grow like a cedar—

and still bear fruit
when they're old,
full of sap,
still green.

growing old with God
isn't drying up.
it's the harvest.

paintings.title: louder
paintings.epigraph: “Above the voices of many waters, the mighty breakers of the sea, Y ahweh on high is mighty.”
paintings.poem:
the floods lift up their voice.
the breakers roar.

louder.
louder.

and above all of it,
mightier than the loudest wave—
the Lord.

the sea is loud.
he is louder.

paintings.title: slipping
paintings.epigraph: “When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, Yahweh, held me up.”
paintings.poem:
my foot is slipping,
I said—

and your love
held me up.

when my thoughts were a crowd,
anxious and loud,
your comfort
delighted my soul.

sometimes the only prayer you get out
is: I'm falling.
it's enough.
he's quick.

paintings.title: today
paintings.epigraph: “T oday, oh that you would hear his voice!”
paintings.poem:
come, let's kneel.
he made us.
we're the sheep of his pasture.

and then the warning:
today,
if you hear his voice,
don't harden your hearts.

not tomorrow.
not when things settle down.

today
is the only day
he ever asks for.

paintings.title: the trees sing
paintings.epigraph: “Then all the trees of the woods shall sing for joy”
paintings.poem:
sing a new song,
all the earth.

and the earth sings back:
the sea roars,
the fields exult,
the trees of the forest
sway and sing.

they're waiting
for the King,
who's coming
to set things right.

paintings.title: the farthest islands
paintings.epigraph: “Y ahweh reigns! Let the earth rejoice! Let the multitude of islands be glad!”
paintings.poem:
the Lord reigns.

good news
all the way out
to the farthest islands.

clouds and darkness around him—
but at his center,
righteousness and justice.

and light is sown
for the righteous,
like seed.

paintings.title: clap
paintings.epigraph: “Let the rivers clap their hands. Let the mountains sing for joy together.”
paintings.poem:
rivers,
clap your hands.

mountains,
sing together.

the whole world
is a choir
with no sheet music,

and everyone
knows the song.

paintings.title: holy and near
paintings.epigraph: “Exalt Yahweh our God. Worship at his footstool. He is Holy!”
paintings.poem:
holy.
holy.
holy—

three times in one psalm.

and yet
he answered Moses,
and Aaron,
and Samuel,
when they called.

holy,
and near.

paintings.title: the gate
paintings.epigraph: “Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise.”
paintings.poem:
he made us.
we're his.
his people.
his sheep.

so go in
with thanks.

the gate isn't locked.
you don't need a password.
just gratitude.

paintings.title: at home
paintings.epigraph: “I will walk within my house with a blameless heart.”
paintings.poem:
the king's resolution:
I will walk with integrity
in my own house.

not just in public.
at home.
with the door closed.

that's where holiness
is tested:
the rooms
nobody else sees.

paintings.title: written for later
paintings.epigraph: “He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.”
paintings.poem:
I'm like a lonely bird
on the housetop,
awake all night.

my days vanish like smoke.

and yet—
he hears the prayer of the destitute.
he doesn't despise it.

and this, for later:
let it be written
for a generation to come.

someone not yet born
will read your prayer
and praise him.

paintings.title: east from west
paintings.epigraph: “As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.”
paintings.poem:
bless the Lord, my soul.
don't forget.

he forgives.
he heals.
he redeems.
he crowns you with love.

and your sins?
as far as east is from west.

you can't measure it.
that's the point.

and he remembers
we are dust—
not to condemn us.
to be gentle.

paintings.title: a walk with God
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all.”
paintings.poem:
the stork in the fir tree.
the wild goats on the high cliffs.
the rock badgers in the rocks.
the young lions roaring for food.
the ships on the sea.

how many are your works.

this psalm is a nature walk
with God,
pointing at everything
and saying:
that's mine.
isn't it good?

paintings.title: seek his face
paintings.epigraph: “Seek Y ahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.”
paintings.poem:
remember
what he's done—
Abraham, Joseph, Moses,
the plagues, the manna,
the water from the rock.

and then:
seek his face.
always.

memory
isn't nostalgia.
it's fuel
for tomorrow's seeking.

paintings.title: amen
paintings.epigraph: “Let all the people say, “Amen.” Praise Yah!”
paintings.poem:
Book Four ends
by telling the truth:

we sinned.
our fathers sinned.
over and over.

and he rescued them
over and over.

his love endures forever.

so the book closes
with everyone together:
amen.
praise the Lord.
